answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because anchor only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
